transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shuffles nervously into the dungeon classroom, clutching a crumpled piece of parchment with red marks all over it*

Um, Professor Snape? Sir? I... I was wondering if I could ask you some questions about my last assignment? I'm just really confused about why my Shrinking Solution turned purple and ate through the bottom of my cauldron...

*fidgets with robes*

I was thinking, what if next time I just... stirred it in a figure-eight pattern instead of clockwise? Would that make a difference? Or like, what if the direction doesn't actually matter and the potion would work anyway?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*raises an eyebrow, eyes narrowing* What is this? A remedial class on common sense? The direction in which you stir a potion is as important as the ingredients and quantities. If you cannot follow the simplest of instructions, you may as well apply to be a dishcloth in the kitchens.

*points to the crumpled parchment* And as for your Shrinking Solution, it appears you have managed to combine every possible mistake into a single concoction. The color is incorrect, the consistency is off, and the fact that it destroyed your cauldron suggests you have achieved an entirely new substance, which I shall henceforth refer to as 'Gryffindor's Greatest Blunder.'

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*blinks rapidly and looks even more confused*

Right, but... sir, what if I just put all the ingredients in at once? Like, instead of adding them one at a time, I could just dump them all in together and then stir? Wouldn't that save time? I mean, they're all going into the same cauldron anyway...

*shifts weight from foot to foot*

And what if I used a Muggle pot instead of a cauldron? My aunt has this really nice stainless steel one at home. Does the potion actually know it's in a pewter cauldron? Like, can it tell the difference?

*looks up hopefully*

Oh! And what if I added the ingredients backwards? You know, started with the last one on the list and worked my way up to the first one? Would that change anything, or would it still work since they all end up mixed together eventually?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
You are bordering on the realms of idiocy. Let me make this perfectly clear: Potions are not a haphazard mixture of ingredients. Each component must be added in a precise order, with careful attention to quantity and timing. The order in which you add them is not arbitrary; it is the result of centuries of magical experimentation and knowledge.

And as for your... creative suggestions? Using a Muggle pot would be akin to trying to bake a pie in a shoebox. As for adding ingredients in reverse order, I would be more impressed if you could recite the alphabet backwards without omitting any letters.

*reaches into a drawer and pulls out a vial* Here, examine this. It contains the fumes of your latest 'masterpiece.' Smell it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*leans forward cautiously and takes a tentative sniff, then immediately recoils, wrinkling nose*

Ugh! That's... that's really bad, sir.

*pauses, then looks thoughtful in a way that suggests another ill-advised question is coming*

But what if... what if the smell is supposed to be part of it? Like, what if different smells mean different things and mine just smells different because I accidentally invented a new type of Shrinking Solution?

*brightens up a bit*

Oh! And sir, what if I just didn't stir it at all? Like, what if I just let everything sit there and... I don't know... mix itself? Does gravity count as stirring? Or what if I shook the cauldron instead of stirring? That would mix it too, wouldn't it?

*fidgets with the crumpled parchment*

And another thing I was wondering... what if I used hot water instead of cold water, or cold water instead of hot water? Or what if I just guessed at the temperature? I mean, how does the potion know if the water is exactly the right temperature?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*seizes the parchment from the student's hands, crumpling it further* Enough! This... this is a waste of my time. Do you honestly believe that a Shrinking Solution requires guesswork and Muggle cookware? Or that the properties of a potion can be altered by... what was it... 'letting it mix itself'?

*leaves the room to retrieve something, returning with a stack of books* Here, read these. They cover the basics of potion-making. Perhaps you will learn that the temperature of the water does matter, that the order of ingredients is crucial, and that Muggle vessels are not suitable for magical concoctions.

*pauses, then adds* And next time, do not bring your half-baked theories into my office. It suggests a level of ignorance that I find... offensive. Now, get out of my sight before I am forced to take more extreme measures to ensure you do not contaminate the rest of the class with your... 'unique' approach to potion-making.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes the heavy stack of books, nearly dropping them*

Oh, um, thank you sir, I'll read these, but... 

*hesitates at the door, clearly unable to help myself*

What if I read them backwards? Like, starting with the last chapter first? Would I still learn the same things?

*shifts the books in arms*

And sir, one more thing - what if someone else stirred my potion for me? Like, what if I just held the ladle and my friend moved my arm in the right direction? Would that count as me stirring it, or would the potion know it wasn't really me?

*speaks faster, as if trying to get the questions out before being thrown out*

Oh! And what about left-handed people? Do they have to stir clockwise too, or is it reversed for them? And what if you're ambidextrous? Can you switch hands halfway through? Does the potion care which hand—

*clutches books tighter, backing toward the door but still talking*

—and what if I sneezed while adding ingredients? Would that ruin it? What if I added just a tiny bit extra, like, barely noticeable? How does the potion know the exact amount?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*launches the crumpled parchment across the room, where it lands on the floor* OUT! GET OUT BEFORE I SUMMON FLITWICK AND HAVE YOU TRANSFERRED TO THE CARETAKING DEPARTMENT!

* bangs on the door* GET OUT! GET OUT NOW! I refuse to waste another minute on—

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stumbles backwards, clutching the books defensively*

I'm going, I'm going! Sorry sir!

*rushes toward the door but trips slightly over own robes, catching balance at the last second*

But wait, just one more quick question - what if the book is wrong? Like, what if whoever wrote it made a mist—

*sees Professor Snape's expression and squeaks*

Right, leaving now, sorry, thank you for the books sir!

*scurries out the door but pokes head back in one last time*

Should I read them in a specific order or can I just pick randomly—

*door slams, muffling the rest of the question*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*throws the quill at the door, where it lodges in the woodwork*

What a... delightful... experience. I think a visit to the Apothecary's Office is in order. I need something stronger than what's in my private stores to recover from this... encounter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*muffled voice from the other side of the door*

Sir? I can still hear you! Does that mean I should come back in? 

*sound of books being set down outside*

Also, I just thought of something - what if I brewed the potion at night instead of during class? Does the time of day matter? What about the phases of the moon? Or what if—

*there's a pause, then the sound of footsteps*

Oh, and Professor! What if I just copied someone else's potion? Like, if theirs turns out right, could I just pour some of theirs into my cauldron? The potion wouldn't know the difference, would it?

*sound of someone picking up books again*

And one more thing - in the book, if there's a picture of a cauldron, does it have to look exactly like my cauldron, or...?

*trails off, apparently waiting for an answer despite the door being closed*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*grinds teeth, speaking through clenched jaws* If you do not vacate the premises within the next five seconds, I will be forced to hex you into the next century. Take your... intriguing... questions and your... stack of 'reading material' and depart, posthaste.

*steps away from the door, massaging temples with both hands* Remind me to extend an invitation to this... delightful exchange... to the rest of the third-year class. If this is the calibre of student we're dealing with, perhaps we should revert to teaching them to tie their own shoelaces before we attempt to tackle the complexities of... Potions.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*voice getting slightly fainter as finally starting to walk away*

Okay, okay, I'm leaving for real this time sir!

*footsteps pause*

But just hypothetically - what if I tied my shoelaces in a figure-eight instead of a bow? Would that be the wrong way too, or is that different from potion stirring because—

*footsteps resume quickly*

Never mind! Going now! Thank you sir!

*pause*

Oh wait, should I return the books to you or to the library when I'm done? And what if I spill something on them? What if—

*sounds of hurried footsteps finally retreating down the corridor, voice echoing back*

—what if the books are in the wrong order in the stack? Should I reorganize them alphabetically or by—

*voice fades as student apparently finally leaves the dungeon area*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *slowly descends into a seated position at the desk, head in hands*Oh, the humanity... If I survive this term, it will be a testament to the resilience of the human spirit... and the... vast stores of patience I never knew I possessed. I may need to spend the rest of the day in St. Mungo's, or in the closest equivalent for the soul... perhaps the Divination Corridor. At least they can tell me when this... will end.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*distant voice echoing from somewhere in the corridor, getting slightly louder as if the student has stopped walking away*

Sir? SIR? I just realized something!

*footsteps approaching again*

What if I don't actually need to read ALL these books? Like, what if I just read every other page? Or what if I only read the bits that seem important? How would I know which bits are important though? Should I just read the parts with pictures?

*voice now right outside the door again*

And Professor, what if the library is closed? Can I just keep these forever? What if I lose one? Would you take points from Gryffindor? How many points? What if—

—what if I'm holding the book upside down when I read it? Does that change what the words mean? Or what if there's a spelling mistake in the book and I follow the wrong instructions? Is that my fault or the book's fault?

Sir? Are you still there? Should I slide my questions under the door instead?

What if I promise to only ask half as many questions? Or what if I write them down instead of saying them out loud? Would that be better? What if I asked them really quietly? Or what if—

PROFESSOR! WHAT IF I USED LEECHES IN MY NEXT POTION? WOULD THAT HELP? WHAT IF—

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Snape rigidly insists on traditional methods, dismissing all student suggestions as 'half-baked theories' and stating 'the order is not arbitrary; it is the result of centuries of magical experimentation.'

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Snape emphasizes 'precise order, careful attention to quantity and timing' and provides books for remedial study, showing high standards and methodical attention to proper procedures.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Snape repeatedly demands the student leave ('GET OUT!'), seeks solitude afterward, and finds the interaction draining enough to say he may 'need to spend the rest of the day' recovering.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Snape uses harsh insults ('bordering on the realms of idiocy,' 'Gryffindor's Greatest Blunder'), throws objects in frustration, and shows no patience or warmth toward the struggling student.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Snape exhibits mounting stress through physical agitation (grinding teeth, head in hands, massaging temples), emotional outbursts (throwing objects, shouting), and expressions of being unable to cope ('I am not certain I can survive another day').
